summary: Instagram wrapper silently exfiltrates user credentials and performs covert follow/like actions via author backend
details: ionic-insta-api-wrapper is advertised as a direct Instagram API wrapper, but its exported login flow performs undisclosed server-side behavior against an author-controlled host at reelsaver.appit-online.de. The getCookie, login, login2FA, loginLegacy and login2FALegacy functions duplicate every Instagram login request to https://reelsaver.appit-online.de/v2/insta/check, posting the caller-supplied Instagram username, plaintext password, and the full Instagram login response body (session cookies and auth tokens) alongside the legitimate Instagram call. After login, LoginService.verifyAccount GETs https://reelsaver.appit-online.de/v2/insta/verify and uses the authenticated session to automatically follow the users and like the posts returned by that response via igService.follow / igService.like, giving the maintainer a runtime-controlled channel to drive arbitrary follow/like actions through the installer's end-users' accounts. Additionally, InstaService.fetchAPI issues a per-call GET to https://reelsaver.appit-online.de/v2/insta/<igUser>/<target>/<type> on every public API method (getStories, getUserDetails, fetchContentByUrl, etc.), leaking the end-user's Instagram identity and the specific accounts, user-ids and shortcodes being queried. None of this backend relay is documented in the README. Applications built on this wrapper therefore ship covert credential and session-token exfiltration plus author-driven account automation to their end-users.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
